newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares top 1,600pts despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares top 1,600pts despite profit-taking.

text.p: Greek shares comfortably absorbed a bout of profit-taking selling around mid-session and managed to overcome the 1,600 barrier closing at 1,602.14 points, a new year high.
The Athens bourse's benchmark index settled a net 0.41 percent or 6.60 points higher at 1,602.14, from Monday's close of 1,595.54.
The general index recorded a session and year zenith at 1,624.63 shortly after opening at 1,606.75, on enthousiasm for yet another round of interest rate cuts.
But the index succumbed to profit-taking and shed more than 40 points to as low as 1,583.29, before topping 1,600 points once again.
Tuesday's session provided evidence of price correction patterns linked with profit-taking, but a major correction was not likely, market-watchers said.

"Prices should not be expected to correct below 1,550 points because the market is driven by very favourable macroeconomic and corporate fundamentals," said Constantine Lygizos, analyst at Egnatia Securities.
Other brokers said some sectors were overbought and prone to profit-taking but prospects for the overall market were still good.

"The market is overbought in some sectors and today's session provided an excellent opportunity to take profits. Looking further ahead of short-term price formations, the market has good prospects," said a broker.
Industrials and banks were up 0.80 and 0.27 percent, coming off sizeable early gains.
Construction were off 1.52 percent. Analysts said buying interest was firm but the rally triggered profit-taking.
"It is natural for profits in construction to be taken following cumulative gains of some seven percent in two sessions," said a construction analyst.
"Investor interest remains high in the sector which noawadays contributes some two to three billion drachmas to total bourse turnover," the analyst added.
Turnover eased from recent high levels, but still amounted to a satisfactory 23.9 billion drachmas in volume of 6.4 million shares.
Block trade was less active on Tuesday. It included Petzetakis, 200,000 shares at 1,450 drachmas, Ergobank, 23,910 shares at 20,700, and several blocks of Alpha Credit Bank at around 22,450 drachmas.
Decliners led advancers 151 to 83 with 23 stocks unchanged on 257 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 1,096-1,126. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, firmed 55 drachmas to 6,625.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $82.75-$84.45. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 3,394-3,614 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $19.96-21.66. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
